rows.title_short:
Setting Standards For The Contracting Of Loans And Grants With Bilateral And Multilateral Partners, Amending For The Purpose Sections 2, 3, 4, 7, And 9 Of Republic Act No. 8182, As Amended By Republic Act No. 8555, Otherwise Known As The “ Official
Development Assistance Act Of 1996”
rows.abstract:
Allows blended Official Development Assistance (ODA) loans as long as they are covered by official national or international instruments in the nature of exchanges of notes, memoranda of understanding, or similar instruments.
Mandates that in the case of bilateral ODA agreements, the donor government shall issue a guarantee covering at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the commercial component of the loan.
Provides the condition that the bilateral or multilateral agency, or international or multilateral lending institution shall ensure the timely release of funds committed by such private or commercial institutions.
Reduces the grant of element from twenty-five percent (25%) to fifteen percent (15%).
Allows Local Government Units (LGUs) to be eligible for ODA loans provided that no contingent lability arising from ODA loans shall be incurred by the national government.
Mandates that all ODA projects shall be subject to evaluation and approval of the NEDA - Investment Coordination Committee.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE MAGNA CARTA OF FILIPINO SEAFARERS
rows.title_short: Magna Carta Of Filipino Seafarers
rows.abstract:
Aims to improve the Filipino seafarers´ working conditions, terms of employment, career prospects and provide opportunities to harness their potentials to the fullest.
Covers Filipino seafarers who are employed or engaged or work in any capacity on board foreign-registered ships and Philippine-registered ships operating internationally.
Provides seafarers the rights to 1.) employment and social rights; 2.) self-organization, engage in collective bargaining and participate in democratic exercises; 3.) education advancement and training at reasonable and affordable costs; 4.) relevant information; 5.) information of seafarer´s family; 6.) public consultation; 7.) against discrimination; 8.) Free legal representation; 9.) appropriate grievance mechanism; 10.) immediate medical attention; 11.) have access to communication; 12.) fair treatment in the event of a maritime accident; and 13.) fair medical assessment.
Requires any person to be 18 years old and above to be employed as a seafarer, medically fit, and trained or certified as competent and qualified to perform their duties.
Mandates DMW, MARINA, AND OWWA to maintain a unified registry of all seafarers in the Philippines which contain the relevant information or data to promote employment opportunities for seafarers.

rows.title_short: Establishing Evacuation Centers In Every City And Municipality
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish an evacuation center in every city and municipality in the country which shall provide immediate and temporary accommodation for people who have evacuated or displaced from their homes due to disasters, calamities or other emergency events such as typhoons, floods, storm surges, drought and other severe climate disturbances, as well as fire, and the outbreak of illness and diseases that present imminent danger to life and property.
Mandates the NDRRMC to be the lead implementing agency of this Act and to make a priority list of LGUs needing evacuation centers. 
Provides requirements for the establishment of evacuation center such as: a.) location designation; b.) structural and building capacity; c.) suitability and capacity of premises; and d.) amenities and accessibility.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT PROMOTING ENTREPRENEURSHIP BY ESTABLISHING A SUSTAINABLE
FINANCING PROGRAM FOR MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES THROUGH THE
PONDO SA PAGBABAGO AT PAG-ASENSO PROGRAM, AND APPROPRIATING
FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Pondo Sa Pagbabago At Pag Asenso Act Or The “ P3 Act”
rows.abstract:
Aims to promote the growth of micro and small enterprises (MSEs) by providing affordable, accessible, and simple financing programs, and initiated means to encourage entrepreneurial activities, and  to ease the constraints and challenges to MSEs, particularly on access to financing. 
Institutionalizes the Pondo sa Pagbabago at Pag-asenso (P3) Fund which shall be lent out to qualified MSEs and shall be accessible through the Small Business Corporation (SB Corp.) and accredited partner financial institutions (PFIs) such as rural banks, thrift banks, development banks, cooperative banks, cooperatives, non-stock savings and loan associations, microfinance non-government organizations or lending companies.
Provides that the loanable amount for individual loans shall be set and regularly reviewed by the MSMED Council which shall not exceed one percent (1%) per month for direct lending, and shall not exceed two and a half percent (2.5%) per month for lending through accredited PFIs, with no collateral requirement.

rows.abstract:
Aims to ensure protection of more Filipino farmers from financial losses arising from natural calamities, plant diseases, and pest infestation, and direct the resources of private sector entities consisting of cooperatives and farmer´s organizations, to invest in agricultural insurance.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE USE OF FINANCIAL ACCOUNTS
rows.title_short: Anti- Financial Account Scamming Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to protect the public from cybercriminals and criminal syndicates who target financial accounts, e-wallets, and other financial accounts, or lure account holders into perpetrating fraudulent activities.
Identifies and defines certain punishable offenses such as money mule, social engineering schemes and economic sabotage.
 Mandates the BSP to have the authority to examine and investigate individual financial accounts, e-wallets, or other financial accounts which are involved in the prohibited acts and other offenses under Section 4 and 5 of this Act. 
Designates the Regional Trial Court as cybercrime court which shall have jurisdiction over the violation of the provisions of this Act including any violation committed by a Filipino national regardless of the place of commission.Mandates all relevant international instruments on international cooperation in criminal matters, arrangements agreed based on uniform or reciprocal legislation, and domestic laws for the purposes of investigations or proceedings concerning criminal offenses related to computer systems and data, or for the collection of evidence in electronic form of a criminal offense, shall be given full force and effect.

rows.title_short: Enterprise- Based Education And Training ( E B E T) Program Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish a national enterprise-based training and education system for the middle-level manpower that is competency-based, including an off-and-on-the job training program and involving the active participation and cooperation of employees, workers, industry, and the government.
Institutionalizes the Enterprise-Based Education and Training (EBET) Program that shall cover practical work-related or workplace-related training programs with compulsory related theoretical instructions and shall include training modalities or schemes.
Mandates TESDA to establish a registration mechanism and assign an office that shall process all EBET program applications, including the applications for registration of civic groups, association, organization, industries, TVET providers, and government institutions which desires to participate in the EBET program.
Grants tax exemptions to all grants, bequests, endowments, donations, and contributions made to and to be used actually, directly and exclusively by the participating training institution.
